claim_scope: Source, publication, license, and one-molecule runtime-feasibility evidence used only to classify learned implicit-solvent candidates against the Route 1 product contract. This is not a hydration-accuracy benchmark, a provider promotion, or a claim about all machine-learned solvent models.

gnnis.decision_reason: The solvent functional is a pretrained chemistry-dependent model fit to explicit-solvent mean-force labels. It is gas-MLIP-independent and does not contain gas MM energy, but it violates the baseline prohibition on a learned solvent correction/retraining. This Route 1 audit establishes no absolute FreeSolv hydration-energy training or validation gate for treating the released raw scalar as an absolute hydration free energy.

license.audit_wording: permissive MIT-family text; metadata labels are not uniform

local_runtime_feasibility_smoke.interpretation: The released model is technically evaluable as a solvent-only scalar with local scalar-gradient agreement at the probed coordinate. This smoke does not test global smoothness, broad force accuracy, MD admission, conformer free energies, absolute hydration free energies, or product admission.

paper.title: A general graph neural network based implicit solvation model for organic molecules in water

source_findings.learned_nonpolar_term: GNN-predicted SASA scale with learned solvent gamma embedding
source_findings.training_target: mean explicit-solvent solute force minus vacuum OpenFF solute force

limitations: The local GNNIS smoke uses an audit-only import shim for optional compiled PyTorch-Geometric dependencies; it is not product packaging evidence.
Only one force coordinate on one molecule is checked in the smoke because the candidate is rejected by the product contract before a broader force gate.
The published QM-to-MLIP transfer analogy is not treated as validation for any MAPLE MLIP.
GNNIS license metadata is not uniform: the repository is classified as MIT-0 while setup.py advertises MIT License; the exact license-text hash is authoritative for this audit.

overall_decision.reason: Both candidates are scientifically relevant learned-solvent research routes, but neither satisfies the no-learned-correction/no-residual Baseline/Product Route contract. Technical feasibility is intentionally not used to weaken that boundary.
overall_decision.retained_route1_baseline: fixed AM1-BCC plus declared physical PB/GB and nonpolar providers added to any compatible gas-phase MLIP

protocol.admission_rule: A technically conservative and gas-model-independent learned solvent term still remains outside the Route 1 baseline when its solvent functional or correction was trained from explicit-solvent or experimental labels.
steps: freeze upstream source, paper, model, and license identities
identify the exact training target and loss from source
identify whether the released energy contains a gas-phase force-field term
identify whether a proposed transfer is a direct learned solvent provider or an explicit delta correction
separate runtime feasibility from product-contract admission

qm_gnnis.decision_reason: The transfer is explicitly a learned delta correction. Its lack of new QM or experimental retraining does not turn it into a fixed physical PB/GB provider. Published QM-GNNIS sums the Torch correction with ORCA/CPCM and is not a direct MLIP solvent provider. Applying the same delta to a gas MLIP would be an unvalidated inference and would violate Route 1 baseline item 6 even if implemented transparently and with local scalar-gradient consistency.
